thread:
Alex Chen: Kicking off planning for the afterglow iteration — need a quick decision on hotfix vs feature cadence. Proposal: 2-day hotfix window for P0/P1 bugs, then a 2-week follow-on that splits 40% bug capacity / 60% enhancements. Thoughts?
Maya Patel: Agree in principle. Can we make the P0 definition strictly customer-impacting (100% loss or data-loss)? P1 = major feature regression or high-severity customer-reported crash.
Samir Khan: +1. FYI customer #287 reported the duplicate-embedding regression, that's P1 by our definition. Linking ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RED-287
Priya Gomez: We should also gate follow-on feature rollouts on no regression in core embedding latency >2x baseline. If embedding latency regresses, pause feature merges until mitigations are in.
QA-Bot: nightly-smoke: 14 failures, 3 new since yesterday. Top failing suites: embed-e2e (4), streaming-regressions (3), auth-regen (2). Full logs: https://ci.redwood/afterglow/17888/logs
Alex Chen: Good catch QA-Bot. For prioritization: put RED-287 and the top 3 embed-e2e failures into the hotfix window. Everything else with customer workarounds goes into the 2-week backlog tranche.
Maya Patel: One nuance — some UX polish items unblock onboarding for a mid-market customer who may expand contract. Recommend we treat those as 'customer-driven enhancements' and reserve 1 slot in the hotfix window if it prevents churn.
Samir Khan: Operationally, can infra support a 2-day hotfix sprint without disrupting Dedicated autoscaling tests? If yes, I'll schedule the canary for the morning after patch.
Alex Chen: Samir please coordinate with eng-infra. If canary fails, we revert and open an incident. If canary passes, we hotpatch to dedicated pools in staggered regions.
Priya Gomez: Let's make explicit launch acceptance criteria for the follow-on wave: (1) No P0 for 7 days post-rollout, (2) Embedding 95th latency within 1.5x baseline, (3) Top customer flows smoke tests green. If any fail, we rollback or freeze rollouts.
Maya Patel: I'll own creating the triage board and labeling rules. Proposed labels: `P0`, `P1`, `P2`, `customer-driven`, `hotfix-candidate`, `deferred-feature`.
Samir Khan: I'll own the canary run and create the rollback playbook snippet: ```step1: deploy canary to zone-a
step2: run smoke (embed + chat)
step3: wait 30m for metrics
step4: promote or rollback
```
QA-Bot: tagging tests: add `smoke:embedding`, `smoke:chat`, `smoke:auth` to the hotfix job matrix.
Alex Chen: Action items: Priya create backlog tranche and publish acceptance criteria, Maya create triage board + labels, Samir schedule canary + rollback doc, QA run targeted smoke and post pass/fail by EOD. We'll reconvene tomorrow 10:00 to lock sprint assignment. :thumbsup:
Priya Gomez: Noted. I'll post the follow-up doc with criteria and initial triage list in the channel when ready.
Maya Patel: Adding one more ask — track estimated engineering hours per bug so PMs can negotiate scope with sales. Small thing but helps prioritization.
Alex Chen: Agreed. Keep estimates rough (T-shirt + hours). Thanks all, see you at 10am.
